findings.benefit: The nested presentation `K[x,y] ≃ K[y][x]` and the exact outer-degree computation are useful for any coefficient semiring (for instance `ℤ`, or an iterated polynomial ring such as `K[z][x,y]` used in base-change arguments), and stating them at Mathlib's own level of generality lets downstream files such as `BGS/HasseWeil/PlaneConstantField.lean`, which currently repeat these presentations at `[Field K]`, instantiate them without adding field structure. It also removes an artificial dependency of a purely combinatorial reindexing on `Field`.

That is a statement about the Mathlib algebra equivalence `Polynomial.Bivariate.equivMvPolynomial`, which is defined for any `CommSemiring`, but the lemma is restricted to `[Field K]`. findings.proposed_change: State the lemma as `theorem bivariateEquiv_symm_natDegree_eq_degreeOf_one (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) K) : ((Polynomial.Bivariate.equivMvPolynomial K).symm f).natDegree = MvPolynomial.degreeOf 1 f`. The existing proof (lines 140-169) should still typecheck, since every ingredient it invokes is available in the `CommSemiring` setting; elaboration should be checked, in particular that the `Unique`/`DecidableEq` instances it builds on `{i : Fin 2 // i ≠ 1}` behave the same.
findings.benefit: Readers of `Polynomial.Bivariate.equivMvPolynomial` get the degree-computation lemma at the same generality as the equivalence itself, so it can be reused for coefficient rings such as `K[X]` (e.g. iterated or base-changed presentations of a plane equation), not only over fields. It also makes the lemma a natural Mathlib-contribution candidate rather than a project-only field-specific restatement.

findings.problem: The statement is about a general tower phenomenon, but it is stated only for the concrete subfield `frobeniusSubfield L p` and inherits the whole `[Fact p.Prime] [CharP K p] [CharP L p] [PerfectField K]` block from line 181-182, none of which is used mathematically. The proof shows this directly: the only special input is the pair of local instances `Algebra K F` and `IsScalarTower K F L` built from `perfectConstantsToFrobeniusSubfield` (lines 279-286); after that it builds `hAE : adjoin K {z} ≤ (adjoin F {z}).restrictScalars K` from `IntermediateField.adjoin_le_iff` and `IntermediateField.subset_adjoin` and finishes with the completely general tower lemma `Algebra.isSeparable_tower_top_of_isSeparable A E L`.
findings.proposed_change: Move and state the result for an arbitrary subfield of `L` through which the constants factor, e.g. `theorem isSeparable_over_adjoin_of_isSeparable_over_adjoin {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] (F : Subfield L) [Algebra K F] [Algebra F L] [IsScalarTower K F L] (z : L) [Algebra.IsSeparable (IntermediateField.adjoin K {z}) L] : Algebra.IsSeparable (IntermediateField.adjoin F {z}) L`, and keep the current Frobenius statement as a one-line corollary supplying the existing `Algebra K F`/`IsScalarTower K F L` instances. The prop of lines 287-297 carries over verbatim, with `hAE` derived from `adjoin_le_iff` plus `subset_adjoin` and the fact that `algebraMap K L = algebraMap F L ∘ algebraMap K F` (from the scalar tower); the exact instance/elaboration details should be checked, since this variant has not been compiled.
findings.benefit: This turns a fact used once for constants in `L^p` into a reusable library lemma about intermediate constant fields, applicable whenever one enlarges the constant field of a rational subfield (e.g. base-change or constant-extension arguments elsewhere in the HasseWeil development). It also shows readers that separability transfer has nothing to do with perfectness or characteristic `p`, and it would let the main theorem `planeCurve_auxiliaryFamily_linearIndependent` obtain its separability instance without exposing the Frobenius-specific instance construction.
